input.summary:
P6 living and kitchen (parts/room-46.mjs): kitchen stove on the west wall (smoker, lit furnace, cauldron, barrels), dining set via diningSet() at 102..103, settee and armchair around a sideboard and table on a brown carpet in the east corner, and the x104 lane kept clear from the front door to the rear doorway.
Two hanging lanterns at y4 (104,16 and 107,17) light the room; on a scratch copy with a stand-in shell, walk is 33/33 reachable, min light 9, no dark cell, and the fit check is OK.
make.sh runs whole with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines for this part; the shell-east walls and floors are not in this copy, so the real verdicts must be re-run after the merge.
left: The real P6 shell (shell-east: floor y1, walls, ceiling y5, windows, door and rear doorway) is not built in this copy, so `$MCD room build.nbt` on the real build reports NO WAY IN and carpets floating over air. I checked the furniture on scratch/test.nbt (scratch/room46-test.mjs lays a stand-in floor, walls and ceiling; scratch/rooms.json sets the entrance to the front door cell 104,2,14). Re-run `$MCD room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "P6 living and kitchen"` after the merge.

The hearth's lit campfire and flue at (109,2,18) and mouth (108,2,18) belong to the chimneys part; the scratch light map did not count the campfire, so the light near the hearth is only an estimate until the merge.
The room's walk verdict uses rooms.json entrance [7,2,12] (plot 0), which cannot reach this room; the room check needs an entrance at the P6 front door, a shared-kit fix.
plan.md checklist not ticked: the row-wide elements (living room, kitchen with stove, dining table per house) are for all eight houses, so none of them is ticked from this part alone.
No beds here; the P6 west bedroom (room-47) carries the beds.

waste.what: Stand-in shell for checking: the P6 floor, walls, ceiling, windows, door and hearth mouth were laid by hand in a scratch script so the room check could run, because shell-east is not built in this copy.
waste.cost: about 25 fill calls and two retries (one wipe bug that cleared my own furniture), roughly 6 minutes
waste.tool: A `mcd room --shell <parts-or-nbt>` option or a `--stub-shell` mode that reads the plan's openings and lays the plain envelope, so one room can be checked before its neighbour parts land.

waste.what: Room entrance: rooms.json fixes the entrance at plot 0's door (7,2,12), so the walk verdict for any later plot needs a hand-edited copy with the entrance moved to that room's door.
waste.cost: one extra rooms file written by hand with its entrance set to 104,2,14
waste.tool: Per-room entrance in rooms.json (or `mcd room --from x,y,z`), taken from the openings table so each room's walk starts at its own door.

waste.what: Cell-by-cell layout: I worked out each furniture cell's coordinates and state (facings for stairs, lit states, pressure plate on the fence, lantern hanging over the lane) by hand, then drew it into the layers() text.
waste.cost: about 15 cells worked by hand, 3 layers, one rewrite
waste.tool: A furniture legend helper that takes a named room recipe (kitchen run, settee, armchair, dining set) and writes the states, e.g. `kitchenRun(g,{x,y,z,facing})`, `settee()`, `armchair()`, plus a lantern placer that picks spots under the ceiling from the light map.

companions.task: Build the settee and armchair from stairs and the coffee table from a fence post with a pressure plate, to a proper sitting height and spacing, instead of me placing each stair facing by hand.
Lay the hearth surround and the firebox outside the east wall so the campfire and mouth at 109,2,18 and 108,2,18 read as one hearth from inside the room.
Check the hanging lanterns and the lit furnace against the real shell (once merged) and confirm no floor cell drops below 8, instead of my measuring on a stand-in shell.
